name: Forehand flick
summary: Attack a short ball over the table with a short, quick forearm and wrist stroke.
whenToUse: Against a short serve or short push to your forehand that is a little high or has light spin.

keyPoints.stance: Step in under the table with your right foot (left foot if left-handed).
keyPoints.bodyAction: Lean in; the body stays quiet and low.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Very short: a few centimetres back, then up and forward.
keyPoints.timing: At the top of the bounce, over the table.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Over the table, close to the ball.
keyPoints.freeArm: Out to the side for balance; never on the table.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow bent, bat close to the ball. Open a little against backspin, more closed against no-spin.
keyPoints.recovery: Push off the front foot back to ready; a fast ball can come back.
keyPoints.anticipation: Read the serve: heavy backspin needs more lift, no-spin needs more forward.

learningPath.task: Watch the step in and the tiny backswing.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along: step in, flick, step out.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did your foot step in before the stroke?

learningPath.task: Flick short no-spin balls to one spot.
Short game: drop or flick depending on the ball.

gamePatterns.situation: A short serve to your forehand that stays a bit high.
gamePatterns.how: Flick it down the line to their forehand or into the elbow.

causes: Contact too late, below the net height
fixes: Open the bat and lift more
Step in earlier, take it at the top
Start the bat next to the ball

troubleshooting.symptom: I'm stuck at the table after
fixes: Push off the front foot right after contact

penholdNotes: Penholders are natural flickers; use the wrist but keep the stroke short.
